auraIntro: Explorer, Small Magellanic Cloud is a dwarf satellite galaxy linked to the LMC by a stream of neutral hydrogen gas.
overview: The Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC or NGC 292) is a dwarf irregular galaxy orbiting the Milky Way at a distance of 200,000 light-years in Tucana.
formation: Formed roughly 6.5 billion years ago, frequent gravitational encounters with the Milky Way and LMC disrupted its original structure.
structure: A dwarf irregular galaxy containing several hundred million stars across a diameter of 7,000 light-years, with low heavy-element metal abundance.
discoveryHistory: Observed by Southern Hemisphere inhabitants for millennia; recorded by Amerigo Vespucci in 1501 and cataloged by Magellan's crew.
observationTips: Visible to the naked eye as a hazy cloud near 47 Tucanae globular cluster in Southern Hemisphere skies.
funFacts: Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered the Cepheid variable Period-Luminosity relationship studying stars in the SMC in 1912, revolutionizing cosmic distance measurements.
Linked to the Large Magellanic Cloud by the 'Magellanic Bridge', a stream of neutral hydrogen gas and young stars.
Possesses low metallicity (heavy elements), providing a window into conditions in the early Universe.

cards.title: Cosmic Distance Key
cards.subtitle: Low-Metallicity Dwarf Irregular Galaxy
cards.body: The Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) holds a historical milestone in astrophysics: Henrietta Leavitt's discovery of Cepheid variables in SMC calibrated the cosmic distance scale.

cards.title: Magellanic Bridge & NGC 346
cards.subtitle: Gas Streams & Active Starbirth Clusters
cards.body: NGC 346 is SMC's brightest starbirth cluster, harboring dozens of massive O-type stars shedding energetic stellar winds.
bulletPoints: Henrietta Leavitt discovered Period-Luminosity law in SMC (1912).
Connected to LMC by neutral hydrogen Magellanic Bridge stream.
Low metallicity mimics high-redshift early cosmic conditions.
